set1.io: Discuss the types of data and their relationship to medical research
set1.q: Why does the level of measurement matter in medical research?
opts: It determines whether the study is primary or secondary
Primary and secondary concern who collected the data rather than how finely it was measured.
It determines the prevalence of the condition
Prevalence is a property of the population rather than a consequence of the measurement scale.
It determines what can legitimately be said about two values
Correct: nominal categories can only be counted, ordinal values can be ranked, and only interval data supports statements about how much two values differ.
It determines whether the measurement is reliable
Reliability concerns consistency on repetition, which is independent of the level of measurement used.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 48

set1.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set1.q: Which question tests the content validity of a depression screening scale?
opts: Are the items representative of accepted symptoms of depression?
Correct, and the sample items make it concrete: sadness lasting more than two weeks, irritability and difficulty sleeping.
Does a high scorer have the affect of a depressed person?
That is a criterion validity question, comparing the score against an observable response.
Would a clinician interviewing the patient reach the same conclusion?
That is a construct validity question, comparing the measure with another measure of the same phenomenon.
Does the scale give the same score on a second administration?
Consistency across administrations is reliability rather than validity.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 54

set1.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set1.q: What is the mean?
opts: The sum of all values divided by the number of observations
Correct, and it is described as the best estimate of central tendency, with the caveat that extreme outliers can pull it away from the bulk of the data.
The middle score, with half above and half below
That is the median, which is unaffected by how extreme the outlying values are.
The most frequently occurring value
The most frequently occurring value is the mode rather than the arithmetic average of the observations.
The difference between the highest and lowest values
That is the range, a measure of dispersion rather than central tendency.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 71

set1.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set1.q: What defines nominal data?
opts: Categories with order but undefined spacing
That defines ordinal data, where one value can be more or less desirable than another.
Categories without any specified order
Correct, with blood group and eye color as examples. Nothing about the categories implies that one is more or less than another.
Values with order and equal defined intervals
That defines interval data, such as blood pressure or weight.
Values that can take any point on a continuum
That describes continuous data, a subtype of interval data rather than a level of measurement in itself.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 49

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: Why is there no clear-cut point where disease begins?
opts: Diagnostic tests are insufficiently precise
Test precision is a separate issue from the fact that the underlying process is gradual.
Disease is often acquired by degrees
Correct, and the progression is laid out as a sequence: susceptibility, then pre-symptomatic disease, then clinical disease, then dysfunction, then death.
Reference ranges have not yet been established
Reference ranges exist; the difficulty is that the underlying change is continuous rather than stepwise.
Most clinical data are dichotomous
Most clinical information is not binary and exists on a continuum, which is part of the same problem.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 74

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: What is random measurement error due to?
opts: A flaw in the measurement process
A process flaw is systematic measurement error, which produces a consistent departure from the truth.
Genuine biologic change representing disease
A real change in the patient is not measurement error at all, and is the one situation calling for intervention.
Chance, with equal probability of being above or below
Correct, and it manifests as a lack of reliability. Systematic measurement error, by contrast, is a flaw in the process and shows as a lack of validity.
Differences between the patients being compared
Differences between patients are interpatient variation rather than error in the measuring.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 65

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: A patient's blood pressure differs between two readings taken at different times of day. Which variation does that illustrate?
opts: Systematic variation, since the condition is known to affect it
Correct: time of day is a known condition of measurement affecting the value, alongside position, smoking beforehand and the white coat phenomenon.
True biologic variation from unknown random factors
Biologic variation is the residual scatter left when conditions are held the same, not the effect of a known one.
Interobserver variation
Only one patient and one measurement condition differ here; no second observer is involved.
Random measurement error
Random error has equal probability of falling above or below the true value rather than following a known condition.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 64

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: What defines systematic variation in clinical measurement?
opts: Known conditions of measurement affect the values obtained
Correct, with blood pressure varying by time of day, after a cigarette, by patient position, or through the white coat phenomenon.
Unknown factors each contributing a small random effect
That describes true biologic variation, which is random rather than systematic.
Two observers reading the same finding differently
Disagreement between two observers is interobserver variation rather than a property of the conditions of measurement.
The measurement instrument being read imprecisely
Imprecision that is random is random measurement error rather than systematic variation.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 64

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What does the example of a sickle cell trait carrier illustrate?
opts: A normal finding can coexist with disease
That is the other half of the pair, illustrated by the point that a normal value does not exclude disease.
Statistical and clinical abnormality always coincide
The example shows precisely that statistical and clinical abnormality can come apart from one another.
Extreme values are always undesirable
Value extremes may be desirable, as at the lower end of the systolic pressure range.
An abnormal finding can exist without the person being sick
Correct, which is one half of a pair: the other is that a normal test does not necessarily rule disease out.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 75

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What does a high-normal value still tell you?
opts: Nothing, since it lies within the reference range
Position within the range carries information about risk even when no threshold has been crossed.
Risk is higher than at the low-normal end
Correct, so a value inside the reference range is not uniformly reassuring: where it sits within the range still carries information.
That disease is present but not yet detectable
A raised level of risk is not the same as disease that is present but has not yet been detected.
That the measurement should be repeated
Repetition is advised for abnormal results rather than for values within the range.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 75

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: Which kind of measurement error shows itself as a lack of validity?
opts: Random error
Random error produces a lack of reliability, since the readings scatter rather than settling in the wrong place.
Intrasubject variation
Variation within a patient is a property of the patient rather than a form of measurement error.
Interobserver variation
Disagreement between observers is its own category rather than the error that undermines validity.
Systematic error
Correct, because a flaw in the process pushes every reading the same way, so the measure is consistently not measuring what it should.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 65

set1.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set1.q: How can the effect of random variation on a measurement be reduced?
opts: By using a different observer
Changing observer addresses interobserver variation rather than random error in the measurement itself.
By calibrating the instrument
Calibration addresses validity, correcting a systematic displacement rather than random scatter.
By taking an average
Correct, because random departures fall on both sides of the truth with equal likelihood, so they cancel as observations accumulate.
By narrowing the reference range
Altering the range changes how a value is classified rather than how precisely it was measured.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 68

set1.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set1.q: Which three types of data does measurement produce?
opts: Continuous, discrete and dichotomous
Those are subtypes rather than the three top-level categories: continuous and discrete divide interval data, and dichotomous is a kind of nominal data.
Qualitative, quantitative and mixed
Those describe research paradigms rather than levels of measurement.
Nominal, ordinal and interval
Correct, and they form a ladder: nominal has categories without order, ordinal adds order without defined spacing, and interval adds equal defined spacing.
Primary, secondary and tertiary
Primary and secondary describe who collected the data rather than how it is measured.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 48

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: Which examples show that extreme values may be desirable?
opts: The higher systolic pressure and lower cholesterol ranges
The desirable extremes run the other way for both: lower systolic pressure, higher high-density lipoprotein.
The middle of every reference range
The point of these examples is precisely that the middle is not always where the best value lies.
Any value two standard deviations from the mean
Distance from the mean says nothing about whether the direction is favorable.
The lower systolic pressure range and the higher cholesterol range
Correct, referring to the lower end of the systolic blood pressure range and the higher end of the high-density lipoprotein range.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 76

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: When should intervention be considered in the face of a changed value?
opts: Whenever the value falls outside the reference range
A statistically abnormal value does not by itself establish a pathological change, and abnormal tests should be repeated.
Whenever the value differs from the previous one
Consecutive values differ routinely through biologic variation alone.
Only when there is a true pathological change
Correct, which is why the source of the variation has to be identified: acting on biologic variation or measurement error means treating something that is not there.
Whenever two observers disagree about the value
Observer disagreement is a reason to resolve the measurement rather than to intervene.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 66

set1.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set1.q: Which pair are examples of continuous data?
opts: Number of children and number of heart attacks
Both are counts, taking only specific values, which makes them discrete.
Blood group and eye color
Both are categories without order, which makes them nominal.
Cancer stage and pitting edema grade
Both have order without defined equal intervals, which makes them ordinal.
Blood pressure and weight
Correct, because each can take any value in a range, bounded only by how precisely the measurement can be made.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 51

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What caution accompanies the discussion of defining abnormality?
opts: Always treat values outside the range
Intervention should only be considered where there is a true pathological change.
Never repeat an abnormal test
Abnormal tests should be confirmed by repeating them, because of regression to the mean.
Be careful of labeling
Correct, because cutoffs are often arbitrary and a statistically abnormal value need not mean the patient is unwell.
Disregard values within the reference range
Position within the range still carries information, since high-normal values carry higher risk than low-normal ones.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 77

set1.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set1.q: Can a measurement be reliable without being valid?
opts: No, reliability guarantees validity
A device consistently reading five units high is perfectly reliable and entirely invalid.
Yes, it can be consistently wrong
Correct, and that combination of low validity with high reliability is the one to watch for, since repeated agreement looks like confirmation.
No, the two terms mean the same thing
Validity is accuracy and reliability is reproducibility; a measure can have either without the other.
Yes, but only when the sample is small
Sample size has no bearing on whether a measuring process is consistently displaced from the truth.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 59

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What does statistical abnormality not necessarily imply?
opts: That the value was measured accurately
Measurement accuracy is a separate question from what an accurate abnormal value means.
That the value lies outside the reference range
Lying outside the range is what statistical abnormality means rather than something it fails to imply.
Practical or clinical abnormality
Correct, with a serum cholesterol of 201 as the example: above the desired level, but not clinically significant in itself.
That the test was performed correctly
Technical performance is a separate issue from the interpretation of a correctly obtained result.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 75

set1.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set1.q: What may inter-patient variation be due to?
opts: Only inherent biological differences
Systematic differences in the conditions of measurement and measurement error contribute as well.
Only differences in how the measurement was taken
Inherent biological differences between people contribute too.
Only errors made by the observer
Observer error is one contributor among several rather than the whole explanation.
Biological differences, measurement conditions, and measurement error
Correct, and it matters because answers to clinical questions about an individual are most often derived from groups of patients with similar conditions.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 67

set1.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set1.q: Which is an example of ordinal data?
opts: Blood group
Blood group has categories with no inherent order, which makes it nominal.
Cancer staging from I to IV
Correct, alongside pitting edema graded one to four plus, patient status or condition, and the drug risk categories for birth defects.
Blood pressure
Blood pressure has order and defined equal intervals, which makes it interval and continuous.
Number of heart attacks
A count has defined equal intervals and takes only specific values, which makes it discrete interval data.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 50

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What does a normal test result not do?
opts: Rule out disease
Correct, which pairs with the converse: an abnormal finding does not establish that the person is sick, as with a sickle cell trait carrier.
Reassure the patient
Reassurance is a consequence of interpretation rather than something a normal result is said not to provide.
Fall within the reference range
Falling within the range is what makes the result normal in the first place.
Require confirmation by repetition
Repetition is advised for abnormal results rather than for normal ones.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 76

set1.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set1.q: What can be said about two ordinal values?
opts: By exactly how much one exceeds the other
The size of the gap is precisely what ordinal data cannot tell you, since the intervals are undefined.
Whether one is more, less or equally desirable
Correct, and what cannot be said is by how much, because the intervals between adjacent categories are not defined or equal.
Nothing beyond that they differ
Ordinal data does carry order; it is nominal data that supports no comparison of magnitude.
That the difference is the same at every step
Equal steps are the defining feature of interval data rather than ordinal data.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 50

set1.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set1.q: What is said about cutoff points for normal and abnormal?
opts: They are derived from measured healthy populations
The normal distribution underlying them is based on mathematical theory rather than actual measurement.
They are fixed by national agencies
They are described as often arbitrary rather than as centrally determined.
They mark the point where disease begins
There is no clear-cut point at which disease begins, since it is often acquired by degrees.
They are often arbitrary
Correct, and the warning attached follows from it: be careful of labeling, since a label applied on an arbitrary threshold follows the patient afterwards.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 77

set1.io: Explain the implications of normal versus skewed distribution
set1.q: By what other names is the normal distribution known?
opts: The Gaussian distribution or bell curve
Correct, and all three names describe the same symmetric shape in which mean, median and mode coincide.
The frequency distribution
A frequency distribution is any portrayal of quantity by category rather than this particular symmetric shape.
The interquartile distribution
The interquartile range is a measure of dispersion rather than a distribution.
The skewed distribution
A skewed distribution is the asymmetric case, in which the mean is pulled away from the median.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set1.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set1.q: What is construct validity?
opts: The measure relates to others believed part of the same phenomenon
Correct, as in whether a clinician interviewing a patient for depression reaches the same determination as a screening test does.
The measure predicts an observable event
That is criterion validity, checked against an external response rather than another measure.
The measure includes every relevant dimension
That is content validity, which asks whether the instrument covers the relevant dimensions and excludes the rest.
The measure produces the same result each time
That is reliability, which concerns consistency rather than what is being captured.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 53

set1.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set1.q: By what two things is a frequency distribution described?
opts: Validity and reliability
Those are properties of a measurement rather than descriptors of a distribution.
Central tendency and dispersion
Correct: central tendency locates the middle of the distribution, and dispersion describes how widely the values are spread around it.
Incidence and prevalence
Those are measures of disease frequency rather than descriptors of a distribution of values.
Bias and chance
Those are sources of error in a study rather than ways of describing data.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 70

set1.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set1.q: What is the net effect of random variation across many measurements?
opts: It biases the result in one direction
Consistent displacement in one direction is what systematic variation does.
It makes the measurement invalid
Random variation affects reliability rather than validity, since the readings scatter rather than settling off target.
It cannot be estimated or reduced
It can be reduced by taking an average and estimated during statistical analysis.
It balances out, so the true state is not misrepresented
Correct, although individual measurements can still mislead, which is why averaging reduces it and statistical analysis can estimate it.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 68

set1.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set1.q: What is the median?
opts: The middle score, with half the values on each side
Correct, and because it depends on position rather than magnitude, an extreme value at one end moves it far less than it moves the mean.
The most frequently occurring value
The most frequently occurring value is the mode, which need not lie near the middle of the distribution.
The average of all the values
The sum of the values divided by their number is the mean, which outliers can pull away from the center.
The range between the 25th and 75th percentiles
That is the interquartile range, a measure of dispersion rather than of where the middle of the data lies.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 71

set1.io: Explain the implications of normal versus skewed distribution
set1.q: What proportion of values falls within one standard deviation of the mean in a normal distribution?
opts: About 95 percent
That is the proportion within TWO standard deviations rather than one.
About two thirds
Correct, and 95 percent fall within two standard deviations, which is where the conventional reference range comes from.
About half
Half the values fall below the median, which is a different statement from the spread about the mean.
Essentially all of them
Values continue beyond two standard deviations, which is why 95 percent rather than all fall within that band.
set1.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What does a frequency distribution portray?
opts: The average value across the sample
A single average is a measure of central tendency rather than the whole distribution.
The spread of values around the mean
Spread is dispersion, one of the two things used to describe a distribution rather than the distribution itself.
The quantity in each category, class or interval
Correct, showing the number or proportion of people with different values. It can be used on nominal variables as well as interval data.
The proportion of people who develop a condition
The proportion developing a condition over a period is incidence rather than a frequency distribution of values.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 69

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What does reliability mean?
opts: The measurement captures what it is meant to
Capturing what the measurement is meant to capture is validity, also called accuracy, rather than reliability.
The result applies to other populations
That is external validity of a study rather than reliability of a measurement.
Repeated attempts produce similar results
Correct, and it goes by several other names: reproducibility, repeatability and precision. Note that none of them implies the result is correct.
The measurement is free of systematic error
Freedom from systematic error is validity; reliability concerns consistency, and a measure can be consistently wrong.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 58

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What does systematic variation do to results?
opts: It balances out over many measurements
Balancing out across many measurements is the behavior of random variation rather than of systematic variation.
It can be removed by taking an average
Averaging addresses random variation; a systematic displacement survives it.
It affects only individual measurements
It affects the overall result, which is precisely what makes it bias.
It biases them
Correct, and unlike random variation it does not balance out with more measurements, so averaging does not help.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 68

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What is criterion validity?
opts: The measure covers all relevant dimensions of the concept
That is content validity, which concerns what the instrument includes and excludes.
The measure predicts or associates with an observable event
Correct, as in whether chronically high cholesterol is accompanied by xanthelasma, which is an outside observation the measure can be checked against.
The measure agrees with related measures of the same thing
That is construct validity, which compares the measure against others of the same underlying phenomenon.
The measure gives consistent results on repetition
Giving the same result on repetition is reliability rather than any of the three forms of validity.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 53

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What does a measurement with low validity and high reliability look like?
opts: Tightly clustered results, all away from the true value
Correct, and it is the most dangerous combination, because the consistency is easily mistaken for correctness when nothing is checked against a known standard.
Widely scattered results centered on the true value
That describes high validity with low reliability: right on average but unreliable individually.
Tightly clustered results on the true value
That is high validity with high reliability, the ideal case.
Widely scattered results away from the true value
That is low validity with low reliability, where the measurement fails on both counts.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 59

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: How can the validity of a measuring device be ensured?
opts: By repeating the measurement several times
Repeating a measurement tests reliability; a consistently wrong device repeats its error faithfully.
By calibrating it against known values
Correct, and where the thing measured is more subjective, structured questions serve the same purpose, as with alcohol screening questionnaires and pain scales.
By increasing the sample size
A larger sample reduces the influence of random variation rather than correcting an inaccurate instrument.
By blinding the observer to the result
Blinding addresses observer bias rather than whether the instrument measures the right quantity.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 52

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: One clinician grades a murmur as three and another grades it as four. Which variation is that?
opts: Intraobserver variation
That would require the same clinician to grade the same murmur differently on two occasions.
Interobserver variation
Correct, because two different observers reached different readings of the same finding rather than one observer differing from themselves.
Intrasubject variation
That would be the murmur itself changing rather than the readings of it differing.
Systematic measurement error
Systematic error is a flaw in the process producing a consistent departure rather than disagreement between two readers.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 60

set2.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set2.q: What is dichotomous data?
opts: Ordinal data with exactly two ranks
Dichotomous data is defined as a subtype of nominal rather than ordinal data.
Interval data rounded to two values
Interval data carries defined equal spacing, which dichotomous categories do not.
Nominal data divided into two categories
Correct, with yes and no, or present and absent, as the examples. It is a special case of nominal data rather than a category of its own.
Data with two possible measurement scales
The term refers to two categories of the variable rather than two scales of measurement.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 49

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What helps establish validity for more subjective measurements?
opts: Structured questions
Correct, with alcohol screening questionnaires and pain scales as the examples, since neither quantity can be checked against a physical standard.
Calibration against a physical standard
Subjective measurements are precisely those with no physical standard to calibrate against.
Taking the average of several observers
Averaging addresses variation between observers rather than whether the right construct is captured.
Repeating the measurement on another day
Repeating a measurement tests reliability rather than validity, since a wrong device repeats its error faithfully.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 52

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What is content validity?
opts: The measure predicts an observable event
That is criterion validity, which concerns association with an external response.
The measure covers all relevant dimensions and excludes irrelevant ones
Correct, and the exclusion half matters as much as the inclusion: a depression scale that also captured unrelated distress would fail on the same criterion.
The measure agrees with others of the same phenomenon
That is construct validity, which compares the measure against related measures.
The measure gives the same result on repetition
Consistency on repetition is reliability rather than any form of validity.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 53

set2.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set2.q: What defines interval data?
opts: Order without defined intervals
Order without defined intervals defines ordinal data, such as cancer staging from one to four.
Categories with no order
Categories with no order at all define nominal data, such as eye color or blood group.
Order with defined, equal intervals
Correct, and it splits into two subtypes: continuous data, which can take any value in a range, and discrete data, which takes only specific values.
Values restricted to two categories
Restriction to two categories describes dichotomous data, which is a subtype of nominal rather than interval.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 51

set2.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set2.q: What stages are named in the progression toward death?
opts: Susceptibility, pre-symptomatic, clinical disease, dysfunction
Correct, and setting them out as stages is what makes the point: there is no single moment at which a person crosses from well to ill.
Exposure, incubation, infection, recovery
That describes the course of an infection rather than the general progression named.
Nominal, ordinal, interval, continuous
Those are levels of measurement rather than stages of disease.
Endemic, epidemic, pandemic, eradication
Those describe the distribution of disease in populations rather than its course in a person.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 74

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What produces true biologic variation?
opts: A single known factor affecting the measurement
A known factor affecting the values is systematic variation rather than true biologic variation.
A flaw in the measuring process
A flaw in the measuring process is systematic measurement error, which is not variation arising in the patient.
Disagreement between two observers
Observer disagreement is interobserver variation rather than variation in the patient.
Many unknown factors each contributing a small random effect
Correct, which is why consecutive systolic pressures taken under the same conditions will not be exactly the same in the same patient.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 63

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What is the mode?
opts: The middle value of the ordered data
The middle value of the ordered data is the median rather than the value occurring most often.
The sum divided by the number of observations
The sum divided by the number of observations is the mean rather than the most frequent value.
The value two standard deviations above the mean
That describes a position in a normal distribution rather than a measure of central tendency.
The most frequently occurring value
Correct, and it is the only one of the three that need not be a value near the center at all, since a distribution can have its peak anywhere.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 71

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What is the weakness of the mean?
opts: It cannot be calculated for interval data
Interval data is exactly what a mean is calculated from, so this is not what limits the measure.
It can be affected by extreme outliers
Correct, which is why the median, defined by position rather than magnitude, holds up better when a few values sit far from the rest.
It ignores the number of observations
The number of observations is the divisor, so it is central to the calculation.
It is the same as the mode in all distributions
They coincide in a symmetric distribution but diverge when the distribution is skewed.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 71

set2.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set2.q: What distinguishes continuous from discrete data?
opts: Continuous takes only specific values
Taking only specific values is what makes data discrete, as with a count of children or of heart attacks.
Continuous can take any value in a range
Correct, though limited by the precision of the measurement, whereas discrete data takes only specific values such as a number of children.
Discrete data has no defined intervals
Both subtypes are interval data, so both have defined equal intervals.
Discrete data has no order
Absence of order defines nominal data rather than discrete data.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 51

set2.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set2.q: Why should an abnormal test be repeated?
opts: Because the laboratory may have lost the sample
The reason given is a statistical phenomenon rather than a handling failure.
Because repeated testing improves validity
Repetition addresses reliability; validity is established by calibration against known values.
Because of regression to the mean
Correct: an extreme value measured once tends to sit closer to the average when measured again, so the first result may overstate the departure.
Because the reference range changes over time
Reference ranges are described as often arbitrary rather than as shifting between one test and the next.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 77

set2.io: Discuss the concepts of validity and reliability and their relationship to measurement
set2.q: What does validity mean in measurement?
opts: Repeated measurements give similar results
That is reliability, also called reproducibility, repeatability or precision.
The results apply to other clinical settings
That is external validity of a study rather than validity of a measurement.
The measurement is free of random variation
Random error affects reliability; validity concerns whether the right thing is being measured.
The data measure what they are supposed to measure
Correct, and it is also called accuracy. It can be ensured by calibrating devices and by comparing results when measuring known values.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 52

set2.io: Explain the implications of normal versus skewed distribution
set2.q: What is the normal distribution based on?
opts: Measurements taken from healthy populations
It is explicitly based on mathematical theory rather than on measured data.
The distribution of disease in a community
Disease distribution is evaluated by person, place and time rather than described by this curve.
The precision of the measuring instrument
Instrument precision limits how finely a value can be recorded rather than defining the shape of the curve.
Mathematical theory rather than actual measurement
Correct, and that is worth remembering before treating a reference range as a fact about bodies: the curve is a model that real data may or may not follow.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What is intraobserver variation?
opts: One observer interpreting the same thing differently twice
Correct, with a radiologist reviewing the same radiograph at two different times and reaching different interpretations as the example.
Two observers interpreting the same thing differently
Two observers reading the same finding differently is interobserver variation rather than variation within one reader.
One patient's value changing between measurements
That is intrasubject variation, arising from the patient rather than the reader.
A flaw in the measuring instrument
An instrument flaw is systematic measurement error rather than observer variation.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 60

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What does the standard deviation describe?
opts: The variability of scores about the mean
Correct, and it is the measure the normal distribution is expressed in: about two thirds of values within one standard deviation, and 95 percent within two.
The full spread from lowest to highest value
The full spread from lowest to highest value is the range, which the two extreme observations dictate.
The middle value of the distribution
The middle value is the median, a measure of central tendency rather than of dispersion about the mean.
The most frequently occurring value
The most frequently occurring value is the mode, another measure of central tendency rather than of spread.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set2.io: Discuss the limitations of differentiating between normal and abnormal
set2.q: In what context should abnormality be determined?
opts: Whatever falls outside two standard deviations
A statistical cutoff of that kind does not establish that a value is associated with harm.
Values known to be associated with disease, disability or death
Correct, together with a clinically recognizable difference from healthy, rather than by statistical position alone.
Whatever the laboratory reports as high or low
Laboratory flags follow reference ranges, and cutoff points for normal and abnormal are often arbitrary.
Whatever differs from the patient's previous result
A change may reflect biologic variation or measurement error rather than a pathological difference.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 77

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What two phenomena combine to produce fluctuation in clinical measurements?
opts: Bias and publication practice
Publication practice affects which studies reach print rather than why a measurement fluctuates.
Sampling and randomization
Those concern how a study assembles its groups rather than why individual measurements vary.
Biologic differences and variation in measurement
Correct, and separating them matters: one describes the patient genuinely differing, the other the process of measuring failing to pin the value down.
Prevalence and incidence
Those are measures of disease frequency rather than sources of measurement fluctuation.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 62

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What three sources can explain variation within one patient?
opts: Bias, chance and confounding
Those are threats to a study's conclusions rather than explanations for one patient's values changing.
Sampling, blinding and randomization
Those are design features of a study rather than sources of intra-patient variation.
Biologic variation, measurement error, and real disease change
Correct, and identifying which is operating is the clinical point: intervention should only be considered if there is a true pathological change.
Incidence, prevalence and case fatality
Those are measures of disease frequency and severity rather than sources of variation.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 66

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What does the range describe?
opts: All values from the lowest to the highest
Correct, which makes it wholly dependent on the two most extreme observations, and is why the interquartile range exists as a limited alternative.
The values between the 25th and 75th percentiles
That is the interquartile range, described as a limited range index.
The variability of scores about the mean
The variability of the scores about the mean is the standard deviation rather than the full spread.
The middle of the distribution
The middle of the distribution is central tendency rather than a measure of how widely values are spread.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set2.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set2.q: What characterizes ordinal data?
opts: Categories with no order at all
Categories with order but undefined spacing define ordinal data, such as cancer stage or edema grade.
Equal defined intervals between values
Equal defined intervals make data interval rather than ordinal.
Only two possible values
Two categories describes dichotomous data, a subtype of nominal.
Order among categories without defined intervals
Correct: one value can be seen as more, less or equally desirable than another, but the distance between adjacent categories is not defined or equal.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 50

set2.io: Discuss variation, distribution, and dispersion in data
set2.q: What is the interquartile range?
opts: The full spread from lowest to highest value
That is the range, which the interquartile range exists to improve on.
The variability of scores about the mean
The variability of scores about the mean is the standard deviation rather than a range between percentiles.
The proportion of values within one standard deviation
That proportion is about two thirds in a normal distribution, which is a different statement.
A limited range index, such as the 25th to 75th percentiles
Correct, and limiting it that way is the point: it describes the spread of the bulk of the data without being dictated by the two extreme values.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 73

set2.io: Identify different levels of measurement in data
set2.q: What limits how finely continuous data can be recorded?
opts: The number of categories chosen in advance
Predefined categories are a feature of nominal and ordinal data rather than a limit on continuous measurement.
The precision of the measurement
Correct. The underlying quantity varies continuously, but what can be recorded is bounded by the instrument and the method used to read it.
The size of the sample
Sample size affects the precision of an estimate rather than the resolution of an individual measurement.
The type of distribution the data follow
Distribution describes how values are spread rather than how finely each one can be measured.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 51

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What does systematic measurement error determine?
opts: A range for the true score
Correct, and that is the practical consequence of a known flaw in the process: the reading is not the value, but it bounds where the value lies.
The reliability of the instrument
Reliability is undermined by random error rather than systematic error.
The prevalence of the condition
Prevalence is a property of the population rather than of the measuring process.
The central tendency of the distribution
Central tendency describes the middle of a set of values rather than the bounds on one true score.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 65

set2.io: Differentiate between the types of variation in disease measurement
set2.q: What is intrasubject variation?
opts: Variation within one person across measurements
Correct, as with blood pressure varying by biological variation, time of day, position and stress, all in the same patient.
Variation between two observers reading the same finding
That is interobserver variation, as when one clinician grades a murmur three and another grades it four.
Variation in one observer reading the same thing twice
That is intraobserver variation, as with a radiologist reading the same film differently on two occasions.
Variation between different patients
Variation between patients is interpatient variation rather than variation within one subject.
set2.cite: 3 PAJ5512 Rates and Measurement MBF_2026sc.pptx, Slide 60
